habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: a large self-clinging, deciduous climber. Trees and Shrubs Online: a deciduous climbing shrub to 15 m or more.

value: extension shoots that creep and cling
side shoots that stand free and do not root
habit.shootKinds.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: far-creeping extension shoots attached by aerial roots colonise the surface; shorter, non-rooting side shoots then grow out from it and carry most of the flowers and leaves, and can become well over 1 m long given time.

stem.internodeLengthM.basis: No flora read gives it. Measured on two variegated sports of this plant for their US plant patents: about 2.5 cm on lateral branches (PP11,038, 'Firefly') and 4 cm on average (PP13,845, 'Kasai'). A sport's figure, entered as an assumption for the plain plant.

stem.youngShootColour.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: current-year branchlets reddish brown, with curled hairs. Virginia Tech dendrology: twigs green when new, turning red, then brown.

stem.youngShootSurface.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan.

stem.barkOld.value: thin and loose, peeling in strips
stem.barkOld.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: bark thin and loose, peeling in strips when old. NC State Extension: shaggy, exfoliating.

stem.barkColour.basis: University of Connecticut plant database: exfoliating, cinnamon to tan, very showy on larger stems. NC State Extension and Virginia Tech: reddish brown. Morton Arboretum: dark cinnamon-brown on mature stems.

stem.barkPeelsFromAgeYears.basis: A nursery note, seen only as a search summary and not opened, says trunks older than four years peel markedly. Entered as an assumption until a source can be read.

holdfast.kind.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: climbs by aerial roots that cling to walls, tree trunks and rocks. RHS: forms aerial roots on its stems.

holdfast.position.value: on extension shoots only, on the side that lies against the support
holdfast.position.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: only the extension shoots bear aerial roots; the side shoots are non-rooting. That they stand on the side against the support is read from photographs.

holdfast.rootletLengthM.basis: Read from photographs: a few millimetres to about a centimetre where they lie on what they hold. Not measured in any source read. The same figures as the growth model's appendages.aerialRootLengthM.

holdfast.colour.basis: US plant patent PP11,038, described from a sport of this plant: aerial roots emerge fleshy in spring, then harden off to dry brown, which helps them attach.

leaf.arrangement.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: leaves opposite.

leaf.pairsOnFloweringShoot.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: leaves in 2 or 3 pairs on current-year branchlets.

leaf.division.basis: NC State Extension: leaf type simple.

leaf.bladeShape.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: blade broadly ovate to ovate-orbicular.

leaf.bladeLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: blade 5.5 to 12 cm long.

leaf.bladeWidthM.basis: US plant patent PP13,845, of the plain-leaved plant its sport arose on: leaves 5 to 10 cm long and 3 to 8 cm wide. Trees and Shrubs Online gives no width.

leaf.bladeWidthShareOfLength.basis: From the same patent's figures for the plain-leaved plant, 5 to 10 cm long and 3 to 8 cm wide: the middle width over the middle length. 'Broadly ovate to ovate-orbicular' (Trees and Shrubs Online) says the same in words.

leaf.stalkLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: petiole 3 to 9 cm. The long stalk is what the name petiolaris refers to.

leaf.base.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: base truncate to shallowly cordate.

leaf.apex.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: apex acuminate.

leaf.margin.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: margin finely and acutely serrate.

leaf.marginTeethPerSide.basis: No source read counts the teeth. 'Finely and acutely serrate' is drawn as a tooth about every 3 mm of margin on a blade of middle size, 36 to a side. Counted on nothing.

leaf.secondaryVeinPairs.basis: Flora of China, as given by Trees and Shrubs Online, for Hydrangea anomala: 6 to 8 secondary veins on each side of the midvein, prominent beneath. No count for the Japanese plant was found; the closely related mainland plant's is used.

leaf.texture.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: blade papery.

leaf.surfaceAbove.basis: NC State Extension: dark green and lustrous above, paler below. Trees and Shrubs Online: glabrous above.

leaf.surfaceBeneath.value: paler, hairy along the veins, with tufts of short white hairs in the vein axils
leaf.surfaceBeneath.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan. Not drawn: the model has one colour for both faces of a leaf.

leaf.colourYoung.basis: A nursery catalogue: leaves light green, becoming medium green.

leaf.autumnColour.basis: RHS plant record: broadly oval leaves turning yellow in autumn. Trees and Shrubs Online: short-lived, a yellowish tint in a mild southern English autumn, rich yellow at best, pale cream after cold nights.

inflorescence.type.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: terminal corymbose cyme with opposite branches, bearing fertile and sterile flowers.

inflorescence.shape.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, comparing the two: the flat heads of H. petiolaris. NC State Extension: flat corymb.

inflorescence.widthM.basis: Across the head, sterile flowers included. Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: 10 to 17 cm across. RHS: flowerheads to about 20 cm across. The growth model's organs.racemeLengthM measures the same thing.

inflorescence.stalkLengthM.basis: NC State Extension: a peduncle of 1 to 1.5 in., in metres.

inflorescence.branchSurface.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan. Drawn as a pale, greyish green on the branches of the head.

inflorescence.sterileFlowerCount.basis: US plant patent PP11,038, of a sport whose flowers it calls typical of the plant: about 10 to 15 white sterile outer flowers. Trees and Shrubs Online: the number varies considerably, from very few to many, so the model also draws a head with fewer.

inflorescence.sterileFlowerPosition.value: round the edge of the head
inflorescence.sterileFlowerPosition.basis: RHS plant record: small fertile flowers surrounded by showy white sterile ones.

inflorescence.fertileFlowersDrawn.basis: How many fertile flowers the finest model draws, set by what a flowerhead may cost to draw. Sources say only 'numerous'; a head in life very likely has more.

inflorescence.openingOrder.value: from the edge of the head inwards
inflorescence.openingOrder.basis: Not stated in any source read. In a corymbose cyme the outer branches are the lower and older ones, and photographs show heads with the outer flowers open round a middle still in bud.

inflorescence.appears.value: with the young leaves, well before the flowers open

inflorescence.afterFlowering.value: ages to brown and stays on the plant through winter
inflorescence.afterFlowering.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: the inflorescences quite quickly age to an insignificant brown. University of Connecticut: dried flower clusters persist. Morton Arboretum: the dried remains of the flower heads provide winter interest.

sterileFlower.widthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: sterile flowers 2 to 4.5 cm across.

sterileFlower.sepalCount.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: mostly of about 4 white, petaloid sepals. University of Arkansas: the sterile flowers average 4 sepals. Three and five occur; the model draws four.

sterileFlower.sepalShape.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: sepals obovate to broadly ovate.

sterileFlower.sepalMargin.basis: US plant patent PP13,845, of a sport of this plant: sepal margin slightly crenate, occasionally entire; apex obtuse.

sterileFlower.stalkLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: on pedicels 1 to 3 cm long.

sterileFlower.colour.basis: RHS plant record: showy white sterile flowers. Trees and Shrubs Online: white, petaloid sepals.

sterileFlower.colourAged.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: the inflorescences age to brown. What they pass through on the way (the model draws a greenish cream) is read from photographs and is not from a source.

fertileFlower.colour.basis: NC State Extension: creamy white fertile flowers. US plant patent PP11,038: off-white. A Polish climber nursery: greenish white.

fertileFlower.calyxTubeLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: calyx tube obconical, 1.5 to 2 mm long, with 5 broadly triangular lobes about 0.5 mm long. The ovary is inferior, so this is the body of the flower.

fertileFlower.petals.value: five, joined at the tip into a cap that falls as the flower opens
fertileFlower.petals.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: the unfolding stamens push the petals away and the fused corolla falls off as a single unit, so the open flower is dominated by its stamens.

fertileFlower.stamenCount.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: stamens 15 to 20. More than 15 is what tells it from Hydrangea anomala, which usually has fewer.

fertileFlower.stamenLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: the longer stamens 3 to 5 mm.

fertileFlower.styleCount.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: 2 ascending styles about 1 mm long, which stay on the capsule.

fertileFlower.scent.basis: NC State Extension: numerous small, fertile, sweetly fragrant flowers. Morton Arboretum and the University of Connecticut also call the flowers fragrant; US plant patent PP13,845: slightly fragrant. The RHS record says nothing of scent, and taxon.json records the plant as unscented.

fruit.type.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: a globose capsule with persistent calyx lobes and styles, splitting at the top between the styles.

fruit.widthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: capsule about 3 mm across.

fruit.colourRipe.basis: Virginia Tech dendrology: a small brown capsule, not showy.

fruit.seedLengthM.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online, after the Flora of Japan: seeds pale brown, about 1.5 mm long, winged all round. Not drawn.
